driver: The decisive quantity is a forward yield from a function fitted on closed interventions whose slope on a continuous competitive covariate differs by the type of instrument released, so a single pooled relationship, though it fits, names the wrong candidate.
driver_concrete: Corrasil's 12,992 t MY2028 gain leads only when the preference slope is fitted separately by instrument (b = 0.01177 for tariff-rate quotas, 0.03290 otherwise) and capped by listed capacity, the fit that reproduces the closed releases within 0.77 percent; one pooled slope (515 percent worst miss) names Halden, and Norvale is barred by an open consultation.
stump: A solver who fits one preference-erosion slope pooled across barrier types (or rates on a competitor flag, or reads preference on the in-force date) files Halden, the market the committee thread's analyst already argues for; the in-house round split Halden against Corrasil.
